final_text:
CAUSE: The send endpoint in `app/routes/sessions.py` never takes the "auth is off" case into account when it decides provenance. The fallback branch only accepts a caller who has a valid dashboard login cookie. With no credentials configured, no caller can ever have one.

Evidence:
- In the send handler (`app/routes/sessions.py`, around lines 903–927), a request with `req.sender` is treated as an agent message. Otherwise the code calls `app.auth.validate_session(request.cookies.get("session", ""))`. If that returns false, the handler returns 403 `SOURCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIRED`. Only if it returns true does it build a `MessageProvenance(origin="user", ...)`.
- `validate_session` (`app/auth.py`, lines 55–62) returns False when the token is empty. It also returns False when `DASHBOARD_USER` or `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` is empty. With auth off, both conditions hold on every request.
- Nothing issues a session cookie when auth is off, and `_make_token` would sign with an empty secret anyway. So `operator` is always False.
- The frontend sends only `{message, scope}`, so `req.sender` is empty. Every dashboard chat message therefore reaches the 403 branch.
- The code that grants operator rights elsewhere does check `is_auth_enabled()` first (`app/routes/portfolio.py`, lines 100–113, and the `app/main.py` middleware). The `sessions.py` branch doesn't.
- `require_operator_session` rejects when auth is off, but that is intentional for quota and control-plane mutations. This send path shouldn't copy that behavior.

I read the code and did not run tests or reproduce the 403.

Recommended fix: in `app/routes/sessions.py`, treat the caller as the operator when dashboard auth is disabled:

```python
from app.auth import is_auth_enabled, validate_session
operator = request is not None and (
    not is_auth_enabled()
    or validate_session(request.cookies.get("session", ""))
)
```

This matches how the other routes behave. When auth is off, the auth middleware in `app/main.py` already lets every request through, so the dashboard user is the de facto operator.

Keep the 403 for the auth-enabled case. A request with no sender and no valid session must still be rejected, so agents can't pass as the user.

Add regression tests for both cases:
- Auth off, no sender: expect 200 with `origin="user"`.
- Auth on, no cookie and no sender: expect 403.

Alternative: have the frontend send an explicit sender. This is weaker, because any client could claim any sender. It would also leave other callers broken.
